course: AP Physics 2 nuclear unit, with the nuclear chemistry of AP Chemistry
curriculum: Nuclear structure: protons, neutrons, isotopes, nuclide notation
Mass defect, binding energy and E = mc²
Binding energy per nucleon and the stability curve
Radioactive decay modes: alpha, beta, gamma
Decay constant, half-life and activity
Exponential decay and logarithms
Fission, neutron multiplication and chain reactions
Criticality: mass, geometry, reflectors, moderation
Fusion
Cross sections and mean free path
Attenuation of radiation through matter
Detectors: ionisation, count rate, efficiency, dead time
Counting statistics and uncertainty
Shielding, dose and radiation protection
Conservation of energy and momentum in reactions
Units and conversions: MeV, u, barns, scientific notation
Order-of-magnitude estimation from givens
Materials: phases, allotropes, alloys, density
Shock waves, compression and hydrodynamics
Experimental method: controls, calibration, systematic vs random error
Isotope separation and enrichment
Penetrating power and range of alpha, beta, gamma
Inverse-square law for radiation intensity
Descriptive statistics: mean, spread, standard deviation
Graphical analysis: semi-log plots and slopes
Pressure, temperature and equations of state
Chemical explosives: energy release and detonation velocity
Timing, synchronisation and simultaneity of events
Dimensional analysis and scaling laws
Criticality safety: administrative limits and controls
